clue.text: Wild revelry after tea? Strange but not, that is, for one in ancient race

indicators.note: the wild revelry comes after the tea, so it follows it in the answer

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
a riot is a scene of wild revelry

indicators.note: the following 'that is' must be left out of the word for strange

parts.note: eerie means strange or uncanny
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A puzzled diner wonders whether a wild party after afternoon tea is odd behaviour for an ancient racer.
explanation.walkthrough: EERIE without IE leaves EER. The definition points to a driver in a Roman chariot race.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver in the chariot races of Rome or Greece was a competitor in an ancient race.

clue.text: 'The point of the moon is…' leads to controversy under Sartrian philosophy

indicators.note: the leading letters of the next four words are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A quoted remark about the moon sparks argument among students of Sartre's existentialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Each horn of a crescent moon is technically called a cusp, its pointed tip.

clue.text: Okay but not quite entirely correct?

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: all means entirely, as in all alone
right means correct

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a passable answer is acceptable even though it is not fully correct.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also nods to the spelling dispute: the one-L form is often called not quite correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay and alright are both informal words of agreement or acceptability.

clue.text: Obstinacy creates innings constructed without modicum of style

indicators.note: constructed signals that the letters of creates and innings are built into a new order
without signals that one letter is left out of that pool of letters
a modicum is a tiny amount, here just the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A stubborn batsman builds a long innings with no flair at all.
explanation.walkthrough: CREATES plus INNINGS has fourteen letters; take away the S of 'style' and rearrange the remaining thirteen.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is a refusal to compromise or change one's view, which is obstinacy.

clue.text: Inherent in fatalism: a nihilistic charm

indicators.note: inherent in means contained within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A fatalist philosophy is said to contain a nihilistic attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck, a lucky charm or amulet.

clue.text: Former member of string quartet losing inclination to get better

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: losing means a word is taken out of the one before it

parts.note: a cellist plays one of the four parts in a string quartet
a list is a lean or tilt, as of a ship

explanation.surface: A musician who has left a quartet loses their keenness and tries to improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclination' looks like keenness but is a ship's lean, LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to outdo others, to get better than them at something.

clue.text: Diaries now and then providing platform where opinions may be aired

definitions.text: platform where opinions may be aired

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, so every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Diaries sometimes give someone a stage for airing their views.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for a speaker at a meeting is a dais, from which views are voiced.

clue.text: Drifting east amid sails flapping around mast top

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the compass letter goes inside
around means the rearranged letters surround the next piece
sails flapping are tossed about, so the letters are rearranged
the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A becalmed sailing boat drifts with sails flapping around the top of its mast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flapping' rearranges the letters of 'sails' so that they go around the top of 'mast' and the compass letter for 'east'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drifting moves without purpose or direction, which is aimless.

clue.text: End of many a space mission making front-page news on descent

definitions.text: End of many a space mission

parts.note: a splash is a newspaper's big front-page story
down means descending

explanation.surface: A returning space capsule makes the front pages as it comes down.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule landing in the sea at the close of a space flight is a splashdown.

clue.text: Prop's swaggering gait

explanation.definitionFit: A strut is both a supporting bar in a framework and a pompous way of walking.

clue.text: Charm ally out of tears

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A charming friend weeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal is the formal adjective relating to tears or weeping.

clue.text: Reconciliation with professional body-builders in court following criminal charge

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay follows the charge in the answer

parts.note: rap is US slang for a criminal charge
pro is short for professional

indicators.note: in means the body-builders go inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: he-men are muscular, body-built men

explanation.surface: Muscle men and a professional reach a settlement in court after a criminal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rap' as a charge is American slang. The surface court is a law court; here it is just its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapprochement is the re-establishing of friendly relations, a reconciliation.

clue.text: Clearly pantomime footwear

parts.note: the transparent shoes worn by the heroine of a Christmas pantomime; clearly hints that they can be seen through

explanation.definitionFit: Cinderella, a staple of the British Christmas pantomime, loses one of her see-through shoes at the ball.

clue.text: Semi-limber freestyle swimmer should be so

indicators.note: freestyle means done in any style, so the letters are freely rearranged

explanation.surface: A fairly supple freestyle swimmer ought to be able to go under water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freestyle' looks like the swimming stroke but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A swimmer needs to be able to go into water, so should be capable of immersion.

clue.text: Man U stew about possible pen

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A Manchester United stew is offered as a possible writing pen.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is Manchester United, the football club. 'pen' is not a writing tool but a female swan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen is a female swan, so a female of this white swan species is an example.

clue.text: Guaranteed missing Old Master will be painstakingly drawn

indicators.note: missing means the next piece is taken out of the word

parts.note: promised means guaranteed
OM is a crossword abbreviation for Old Master

explanation.surface: An art dealer warns that a vouched-for painting lacking its Old Master will need careful drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn' suggests sketching but means pulled out with effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prised out has been levered or pulled out with effort, drawn out with difficulty.

clue.text: Hot topic is man-size Kleenex packet finally running out

parts.note: man-size means big

indicators.note: running out means that letter leaves the word

parts.note: Kleenex is a brand of paper tissue

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A box of large tissues running out becomes a hot topic.
explanation.walkthrough: TISSUE without T leaves ISSUE. The surface plays on Kleenex Mansize tissues.
explanation.definitionFit: A big issue is a major matter of public concern, a hot topic.

clue.text: With Tottenham's fifth, no exclamation of disgust is sufficient

indicators.note: the fifth letter of Tottenham is taken

parts.note: taken as written
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A football fan grumbles that a fifth goal for Tottenham, with no disgusted shout, is plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: Tottenham Hotspur is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means as much as is needed, sufficient.

clue.text: Rating from previous season?

parts.note: old means previous, as in an old address
to salt is to season food

explanation.surface: A ranking is drawn from last season's results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' looks like a time of year but is the verb meaning flavour. A rating is a non-officer sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A rating is an ordinary sailor, and an experienced sailor is called an old salt.

clue.text: Laurel and Hardy's separate starts in knockabout comic western — a ready source of money

indicators.note: knockabout means boisterous and rough, so the letters are knocked about
the starts of the two names are taken separately

explanation.surface: Laurel and Hardy make separate starts in a slapstick comedy western that rakes in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: L and H (the starts of Laurel and Hardy) are mixed with COMIC to give MILCHCO.
explanation.definitionFit: A milch cow is a cow kept for milk, figuratively a dependable source of income.

clue.text: Senior officer getting on top of honey-trap's budget

indicators.note: in a down answer, the officer is placed above the next piece

parts.note: CO is a commanding officer
a honey-trap is a sting operation

explanation.surface: A senior officer gets on top of the budget for a honey-trap operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A costing is an estimate of what something will cost, a budget.

clue.text: One stands serene revelling in inactivity

indicators.note: revelling means making merry, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stands calm and content, enjoying doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentariness is a state of sitting about and taking little exercise, inactivity.

clue.text: Benefit from a reported cover-up

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: a veil is a covering for the face

explanation.surface: Someone gains from a cover-up that was reported in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns VEIL into its sound-alike spelling VAIL, after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or benefit, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Cooped up in pup tent, badly put out

indicators.note: badly signals the letters are jumbled
out signals that the letters of the word put are taken out

explanation.surface: A camper confined in a small tent is badly inconvenienced.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove P, U, T from PUPTENT and P E N T remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pent, as in pent-up, describes being shut in or confined.

clue.text: Support in advance of Kasabian's first record with commercials a source of friction

indicators.note: the support comes ahead of the rest of the wordplay

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

indicators.note: the first letter of the band's name is taken

parts.note: EP is an extended-play record
ads are commercials

explanation.surface: Kasabian, a British rock band, release a record with commercials that cause a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'friction' suggests a quarrel but means the rubbing of a vehicle's brakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Brake pads press on a disc to slow a vehicle, so they generate friction.

clue.text: Enforced absence from former French island

parts.note: ex means former
île is the French word for island

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler is banished from a former French island.
explanation.definitionFit: Exile is being barred from one's homeland, an enforced absence.

clue.text: Rough sea suppressing last bit of interest in food

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down, so the rearranged letters hold the next letter inside
rough sea is churned up, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Rough seas dampen the passengers' appetite.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is an informal word for food.

clue.text: What drunks do nightly?

parts.note: drunks are tight, so the bedtime wish describes them literally

explanation.definitionFit: The bedtime farewell wishes someone a sound night's rest; tight here also means drunk.
